svg.title: The 440-Mile Western Front: Trench Stalemate, Verdun & The Somme (1914–1918)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 9 1:10m historical GIS atlas map of the entire 440-mile Western Front from Nieuwpoort on the Belgian North Sea coast down through Ypres, the Somme, Compiègne, the Marne, and Fortress Verdun to the Neutral Swiss border, showing Allied France, SE England, German-occupied Belgium, Luxembourg and north-eastern France, the 1914 German Empire including Alsace-Lorraine, Neutral Netherlands, and Neutral Switzerland.

text.tspan: Sweep halted at Marne; 440-mi trenches to North Sea
Flooded Flanders clay, poison gas (Apr 1915) & mud
10-month German assault forces early Somme attack
Allied all-arms advance forces 11 Nov 1918 Armistice

g.text: Unbroken trenches from Belgian North Sea coast to Switzerland

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: THE GREAT WAR (1914–1918)
The 440-Mile Western Front: Trench Stalemate, Verdun & The Somme (1914–18)
Machine guns, barbed wire & heavy artillery ended mobile war in 1914, locking armies into 440 miles of trenches from Belgium to Switzerland.
After 57,470 British Day-1 casualties on the Somme (1 July 1916), Allied combined-arms tactics (tanks, aircraft & creeping barrages) won in 1918.
